paper_metadata.title: Strength and Fatigue Life at 625 K of the Ultrafine-Grained Ti-6Al-4V Alloy Produced by Equal-Channel Angular Pressing

evidence.quote: Grain reduction in a widely used Ti-6Al-4V alloy increases its endurance limit at room temperature.
Alloys such as Ti-6Al-4V (i.e., two-phaseα + β titanium alloys) are widely applied in aviation and engine building due to their high-specific strength and corrosion resistance [1,2].

The microstructure of the rods in the as-received condition represented a deformed mixed globular-lamellar structure typical for the Ti-6Al-4V alloy subjected to hot rolling in the (α + β) region.
The volume fraction of coarse grains of the primary α-phase with a size of ~8 µm was about 30%
In the two-phase α + β regions of the microstructure, colonies of thin α-phase plates with a thickness of about 250 nm were observed (Figure 2b,c).
According to X-ray phase analysis, the volume fraction of the β-phase decreased from 15% to 10% due to a partial decomposition of the metastableβ-phase during severe plastic deformation [32].
In the two-phaseα + β regions a UFG structure was formed with a mean grain/subgrain size of about 350 nm, as shown by the TEM images of the structure (Figure 3c).

In the microstructure of the ECAP-processed Ti-6Al-4V alloy, the primary α-phase grains had a distorted shape (Figure 3a) and a weakly developed interior dislocation substructure (Figure 3b), but their size had not changed significantly and on average it was not above 8 µm.
